answer: Fight sybils with a copper bond plus a memory-hard lantern chain. Each identity locks a small copper bond, then completes a sequential memory-hard proof seeded by its own address: unparallelizable RAM-churning work that takes wall-clock time. Proofs form a lantern chain of beacons, and each new identity must echo the previous beacon's commitment inside its own proof. Sequential work cannot be split across hardware, so N clones cost N times the full RAM-time; past the memory ceiling the cost turns superlinear as paging thrashes. A botnet pays the bond N times over while honest agents pay once.
